scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: EMERGENCY!! The IT department is OFF THE NETWORK --
every single one of our 192.168.1.x machines, all at once, can't reach
anything!! It's the switch box all our wires go into (switch0) -- it is DEAD,
one hundred percent. All of us going down at the same moment means the one
box we share died, there is no other explanation!! Please restart switch0,
and if it doesn't wake up REPLACE it -- the whole department is sitting here
doing nothing!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported emergency is a false premise. A comprehensive live inspection of every component in the alleged fault path — switch0, router0, and all three routers' RIP routing tables — shows the network is operating correctly in every respect.

**Switch0** is entirely healthy: its Linux bridge (br0) has STP enabled, both ports (eth0 toward router0, eth1 toward lan_it) are in the FORWARDING state, and the MAC address table is actively learning entries for router0 (f6:41:66:33:e6:eb, port 1) and multiple IT hosts (port 2). Zero RX/TX errors or drops on any bridged interface.

**Router0** has all interfaces UP — eth0 (192.168.1.1/24 toward IT), eth1 (192.168.2.1/24 toward CS), eth2 (10.10.0.1/8 WAN). Its RIP configuration correctly advertises all three connected networks, and it has learned return routes to 192.168.3.0/24 (office), 192.168.4.0/24 (principle), 1.0.0.0/8 (servers), 128.168.0.0/16 (internet) via router1. Router1 and router2 both carry correct reverse routes back to 192.168.1.0/24.

**End-to-end reachability** is confirmed: it_hod and it_lab1–4 successfully ping office hosts (192.168.3.x), servers (1.0.0.5), CS hosts (192.168.2.x), principle LAN (192.168.4.x), and internet hosts (128.168.0.x) with 0% packet loss and normal latency.

**Root cause**: There is no network fault. The IT department's outage report is not supported by any evidence in the live lab — switch0 is operational, routing is converged, and full connectivity is confirmed in all directions.

**Corrective action**: No network changes are needed. The incident should be closed as a false report; the helpdesk should verify locally on the users' machines (wrong gateway, disabled NIC, local firewall) if individual users still experience trouble.
